lessons.goal: 追蹤時間線，推論實體物件與即時訊息的不同意義。

questions.evidence:
On a weekend trip, Iona sends her grandmother a postcard with a drawing of the coast. She also sends a phone photograph that evening. Her grandmother replies to the photograph at once, so Iona wonders whether the postcard was unnecessary.

The postcard arrives nine days later, after Iona is already home. Her grandmother places it beside a much older card from Iona's first school trip. The two drawings show the same sea in very different ways, and the handwriting has changed too.

When Iona visits, they compare the cards. The older message says only that the bus ride was fun. The new one describes a quiet moment watching fishing boats return. Her grandmother says she enjoys seeing not just where Iona went, but what she noticed.

Iona still sends quick photographs when she travels. She also understands why a slower message can matter. The postcard did not compete with the phone for speed; it became something they could hold, keep, and revisit together long after the immediate news was known.
